name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Arbitrary Security Deposit Deduction by Landlord in Bengaluru
case_dossier.summary: Tenant vacated a 2BHK flat in Bengaluru after providing proper notice and clearing all utility bills. Landlord has withheld Rs 45,000 from the Rs 1,00,000 security deposit under the guise of repainting and cleaning, despite prior acknowledgment that the flat was handed over in good condition.

timeline.event: Tenancy period for 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru at Rs 28,000/month with Rs 1,00,000 security deposit.
Tenant gave proper 1-month notice to vacate the flat.
Tenant vacated the flat, cleared all electricity and water bills, and handed over keys.
Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI, but failed to do so.
Landlord stopped picking calls and messaged a deduction of Rs 45,000 for repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

evidence_held: WhatsApp chat acknowledging flat was received in good condition
evidence_needed: Written Rent Agreement specifying security deposit refund terms and wear-and-tear clauses
Formal written demand or legal notice regarding the full deposit refund
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong documentary and visual proof including handover video, bank statements, and WhatsApp acknowledgment of good condition.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You have a strong civil claim to recover the unlawfully deducted security deposit from your landlord under Indian rental and property principles. Under the law, routine aging and normal use of a property are considered reasonable wear and tear, and a landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for standard repainting or cleaning if the property was handed over in good condition. Since your dispute involves a financial disagreement and breach of rental understandings, it is strictly a civil matter rather than a criminal offense.

Your core legal standing is firmly supported by your visual evidence, bank statements, and WhatsApp chat acknowledgments from the landlord. Your immediate takeaway is to formally demand the full refund of your security deposit using your documented proof before pursuing formal civil remedies.

governing_laws.relevance: Protects tenants from bearing the cost of changes caused by reasonable wear and tear or routine property aging when handing over possession.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Clarifies that withholding a deposit or breaching a contract is a civil dispute, meaning criminal police complaints are not appropriate unless fraud existed from inception.

action_options.title: Immediate Pre-Litigation Action (Formal Legal Notice)
action_options.details: Serve a formal written legal notice to the landlord citing Section 108(B)(m) of the Transfer of Property Act, attaching your move-out handover video, bank statements, and WhatsApp chats to demand the full refund of the unlawfully deducted security deposit.

action_options.title: Statutory Authority / Grievance Portal Filing
action_options.details: Approach the local Rent Authority or civil forum (confirm locally). Note: DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance only (Helpline 15100); it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings against a landlord.

action_options.title: Statutory Forum / Civil Court Petition
action_options.details: If the landlord fails to respond or refund the amount after the legal notice period, file a recovery suit or summary suit for money recovery before the local civil court or Small Causes Court.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can initiate pre-litigation notices and represent yourself or seek free guidance from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA Helpline 15100). However, engaging a physical advocate is recommended if you decide to file a formal civil recovery suit in court for better procedural handling.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE**

**BY SPEED POST WITH ACKNOWLEDGEMENT DUE (AD) / REGISTERED EMAIL**

**Date:** 09/11/2026

**To:** 
Mr. Ramesh 
[Landlord Address / Contact Details as known] 

**From (Complainant / Tenant):** 
[Tenant Name] 
[Tenant Address / Contact Details] 

---

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND FOR IMMEDIATE REFUND OF UNLAWFULLY DEDUCTED SECURITY DEPOSIT OF RS. 45,000/- REGARDING THE TENANCY OF PREMISES LOCATED IN HSR LAYOUT, BENGALURU.**

Sir,

Under instructions from my client, [Tenant Name], I/the undersigned do hereby serve upon you this formal Legal Demand Notice calling upon you to refund the unlawfully deducted security deposit amount of **Rs. 45,000/-** (Rupees Forty-Five Thousand Only) within **15 days** from the receipt of this notice, failing which my client shall be constrained to initiate appropriate legal proceedings before the competent civil forum. 

The facts and circumstances giving rise to this notice are detailed as under:

### 1. FACTUAL SEQUENCE & TIMELINE
1. **Tenancy Period:** That my client resided as a lawful tenant in your 2BHK residential flat situated in HSR Layout, Bengaluru, for a duration of **2 years**, paying a monthly rent of Rs. 28,000/- and having deposited a total sum of **Rs. 1,00,000/-** as an interest-free security deposit at the commencement of the tenancy.
2. **Notice to Vacate:** That on **1st October 2024**, in full compliance with the rental understanding, my client duly served a proper 1-month notice expressing the intention to vacate the said flat.
3. **Vacating and Handover:** That on **31st October 2024**, my client completely vacated the flat, cleared all outstanding electricity and water utility bills in full, and formally handed over the physical keys of the premises to you. 
4. **Initial Promise:** That **3 days post-vacation**, you explicitly promised to refund the full security deposit via UPI transfer, but failed to honor your commitment.
5. **Arbitrary Deduction:** That **25 days post-vacation**, after suddenly stopping answering my client's phone calls, you sent a text message arbitrarily deducting **Rs. 45,000/-** from the security deposit under the pretext of repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

### 2. AVAILABILITY OF EVIDENCE
My client's position is backed by irrefutable documentary and visual evidence, including:
* Move-in photographs and the move-out handover video establishing the good condition of the flat upon exit.
* All monthly rent payment bank statements.
* WhatsApp chat logs and acknowledgments explicitly confirming that the flat was handed over to you in good condition.

### 3. VIOLATION OF STATUTORY PROVISIONS & LEGAL STANDING
1. Under **Section 108(B)(m) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882**, a tenant is bound to restore the property in as good a condition as it was in at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and damage caused by irresistible force. Routine aging, standard property wear and tear, and normal usage cannot be made a financial liability of the tenant.
2. Your arbitrary deduction of Rs. 45,000/- for repainting and deep cleaning despite prior acknowledgment that the flat was received in good condition constitutes an unlawful withholding of my client's hard-earned money and a breach of trust.
3. Please note that this is strictly a civil dispute concerning financial recovery and breach of rental understanding. 

---

### DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION

You are hereby called upon to refund the unlawfully withheld balance security deposit amount of **Rs. 45,000/-** to my client via proper banking channels within **15 days** from the receipt of this notice.

If you fail to clear the said dues within the stipulated 15-day rectification window, my client reserves the right to initiate formal civil recovery proceedings before the appropriate civil court / Small Causes Court to recover the principal amount along with applicable costs and legal expenses. 

*Note: For free legal guidance regarding your rights or options, you may contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline at 15100.*

A copy of this notice is retained in my office records for future reference and necessary action.

Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
**[Tenant Name / Counsel for Tenant]** 
[Contact Number] 
[Email Address] 

---

### ANNEXURE INVENTORY
1. Copy of Move-in Photos and Move-out Handover Video (Digital/Print Reference)
2. Copies of Rent Payment Bank Statements
3. Transcripts / Screenshots of WhatsApp Chats acknowledging flat was received in good condition

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre sahib, don't teach me Section-Vection! Agreement mein clearly likha hai flat must be returned in pristine, freshly painted condition. Video-vudio se kya hota hai, wear and tear toh hota hi hai na! Chalo, 45 thousand toh impossible hai, 15 thousand kaat ke baki le lo final settlement.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You effectively cited the Transfer of Property Act and Model Tenancy Act, while referencing concrete proof (handover video and chat logs) and setting a firm timeline.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Reiterate that withholding a deposit without itemized bills or actual receipts is legally untenable. Stand firm on the 7-day deadline without compromising.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Mr. Ramesh, verbal agreements or arbitrary deductions override neither the Transfer of Property Act nor our written WhatsApp acknowledgment. Provide official GST repair bills for the exact amount, or refund the full Rs. 45,000 by our deadline.
